dropped.1: Pre-release: TRANSCRIBING_PLACEHOLDER moved to @alexkroman1/aai-ui/internal. It is a tuning constant referenced by no public signature and named by no file outside this package, so it sat in a client.tsx author's autocomplete beside useSession while being a framework decision with no field to set.

Pre-release: DEFAULT_PROGRESS_POLL_MS, DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_POLL_MS and MAX_MISSING_READS moved to @alexkroman1/aai-ui/internal. All three are tuning numbers referenced by no public signature and named by no file outside this package; the hooks that own them take the interval as an OPTION, which is the authoring surface for the same choice and stays public.
dropped.2: The workflow hooks' type parameter is the workflow DEFINITION, not its output type. Epoch 2's `useWorkflowSubmit<Digest>("digest")` no longer compiles: the parameter is constrained to `AnyWorkflowDef`, deliberately, so passing an output type is a compile error rather than a silent loss of typing. What it buys is the other half of the contract — `submit(input)` was `unknown`, so `submit({ ur1: 42 })` compiled and arrived as a 400 in the browser while the same statement already derived the OUTPUT from the def. Migration is one token per call site: `<Digest>` becomes `<typeof digest>`, and the `WorkflowOutputOf` alias above it is deleted.
dropped.3: The workflow hooks' def type parameter is REQUIRED — there is no `unknown` fallback for an un-parameterized call. It existed so `useWorkflowSubmit("digest")` kept compiling, and it was the last way to get an untyped `submit` back. A workflow that declares no input schema now gets `submit(): void` rather than an unusable `never` parameter.
dropped.4: Pre-release: the SDK has no external consumers, so no superseded authoring style is owed a compiling example. A workflow that declares no input schema gets `submit(undefined)` rather than `submit()`: `void` would let the argument be omitted, and Biome's `noConfusingVoidType` rejects it outside a return or type-parameter position.
dropped.5: Pre-release: `SubmitInputOf` and `WorkflowInputOf` are ADDED to the barrel, so this epoch would in fact still compile. Dropped rather than retained because this package has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty. `SubmitInputOf` is in both submit hooks' return type and had nowhere to click; `WorkflowInputOf` was the missing half of a pair whose other half was already re-exported here. `SubmitOutputOf` came off in the same change — it was `WorkflowOutputOf` spelled a second way.
dropped.6: `useRunKey` is purely additive, but `UseWorkflowStreamOptions` narrowed in the same change to `Omit<UseWorkflowSubmitOptions, "wait" | "recover">` — so epoch 6 client code that passed `recover` to a stream submit no longer compiles. No external consumer exists to keep an epoch-6 template for, and aai-ui has dropped every prior epoch on the same grounds.
